   102→    separate thread, when the wrapper is called.

   119→            the wrapped callable will be scheduled to run serially in a

   223→def async_to_sync(
   224→    coroutine: Callable[..., Awaitable[Result]], *args: Any, **kwargs: Any
   225→) -> Result:
   226→    """Invoke a coroutine function from a synchronous caller.
   227→
   228→    This method can be used to invoke an asynchronous task from a synchronous
   229→    context. The coroutine will be scheduled to run on the current event
   230→    loop for the current OS thread. If an event loop is not already running,
   231→    one will be created.
   232→
   233→    Warning:
   234→        Executing async code in this manner is inefficient since it involves
   235→        synchronization via threading primitives, and is intended primarily for
   236→        testing, prototyping or compatibility purposes.
   237→
   238→    Note:
   239→        On Python 3.11+, this function leverages a module-wide
   240→        ``asyncio.Runner``.
   241→
   242→    Args:
   243→        coroutine: A coroutine function to invoke.
   244→        *args: Additional args are passed through to the coroutine function.
   245→
   246→    Keyword Args:
   247→        **kwargs: Additional args are passed through to the coroutine function.
   248→    """
   249→    return _active_runner().run(coroutine(*args, **kwargs))

   252→def runs_sync(coroutine: Callable[..., Awaitable[Result]]) -> Callable[..., Result]:
   253→    """Transform a coroutine function into a synchronous method.
   254→
   255→    This is achieved by always invoking the decorated coroutine function via
   256→    :meth:`async_to_sync`.
   257→
   258→    Warning:
   259→        This decorator is very inefficient and should only be used for adapting
   260→        asynchronous test functions for use with synchronous test runners such
   261→        as ``pytest`` or the ``unittest`` module.
   262→
   263→        It will create an event loop for the current thread if one is not
   264→        already running.
   265→
   266→    Args:
   267→        coroutine: A coroutine function to masquerade as a synchronous one.
   268→
   269→    Returns:
   270→        callable: A synchronous function.
   271→    """
   272→
   273→    @wraps(coroutine)
   274→    def invoke(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
   275→        return async_to_sync(coroutine, *args, **kwargs)
   276→
   277→    return invoke

    61→        return await method(client, *args, **kwargs)

    63→    alias = async_alias if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(method) else alias
    64→

    66→        version_added

    68→    if replace_name:

   167→class _ResultBase:
   168→    """Base class for the result of a simulated request.
   169→
   170→    Args:
   171→        status (str): An HTTP status string, including status code and
   172→            reason string
   173→        headers (list): A list of (header_name, header_value) tuples,
   174→            per PEP-3333
   175→
   176→    Attributes:
   177→        status (str): HTTP status string given in the response
   178→        status_code (int): The code portion of the HTTP status string
   179→        headers (CaseInsensitiveDict): A case-insensitive dictionary
   180→            containing all the headers in the response, except for
   181→            cookies, which may be accessed via the `cookies`
   182→            attribute.
   183→
   184→            Note:
   185→
   186→                Multiple instances of a header in the response are
   187→                currently not supported; it is unspecified which value
   188→                will "win" and be represented in `headers`.
   189→
   190→        cookies (dict): A dictionary of
   191→            :py:class:`falcon.testing.Cookie` values parsed from the
   192→            response, by name.
   193→
   194→            The cookies dictionary can be used directly in subsequent requests::
   195→
   196→                client = testing.TestClient(app)
   197→                response_one = client.simulate_get('/')
   198→                response_two = client.simulate_post('/', cookies=response_one.cookies)
   199→
   200→        encoding (str): Text encoding of the response body, or ``None``
   201→            if the encoding can not be determined.
   202→    """
   203→
   204→    def __init__(self, status, headers):
   205→        self._status = status
   206→        self._status_code = int(status[:3])
   207→        self._headers = CaseInsensitiveDict(headers)
   208→
   209→        cookies = http_cookies.SimpleCookie()
   210→        for name, value in headers:
   211→            if name.lower() == 'set-cookie':
   212→                cookies.load(value)
   213→
   214→        self._cookies = dict(
   215→            (morsel.key, Cookie(morsel)) for morsel in cookies.values()
   216→        )
   217→
   218→        self._encoding = helpers.get_encoding_from_headers(self._headers)
   219→
   220→    @property
   221→    def status(self) -> str:
   222→        return self._status
   223→
   224→    @property
   225→    def status_code(self) -> int:
   226→        return self._status_code
   227→
   228→    @property
   229→    def headers(self) -> CaseInsensitiveDict:
   230→        # NOTE(kgriffs): It would probably be better to annotate this with
   231→        #   a generic Mapping[str, str] type, but currently there is an
   232→        #   incompatibility with Cython that prevents us from modifying
   233→        #   CaseInsensitiveDict to inherit from a generic MutableMapping
   234→        #   type. This might be resolved in the future by moving
   235→        #   the CaseInsensitiveDict implementation to the falcon.testing
   236→        #   module so that it is no longer cythonized.
   237→        return self._headers
   238→
   239→    @property
   240→    def cookies(self) -> Dict[str, Cookie]:
   241→        return self._cookies
   242→
   243→    @property
   244→    def encoding(self) -> str:
   245→        return self._encoding

   248→class ResultBodyStream:
   249→    """Simple forward-only reader for a streamed test result body.
   250→
   251→    Args:
   252→        chunks (list): Reference to a list of body chunks that may
   253→            continue to be appended to as more body events are
   254→            collected.
   255→    """
   256→
   257→    def __init__(self, chunks: Sequence[bytes]):
   258→        self._chunks = chunks
   259→        self._chunk_pos = 0
   260→
   261→    async def read(self) -> bytes:
   262→        """Read any data that has been collected since the last call.
   263→
   264→        Returns:
   265→            bytes: data that has been collected since the last call,
   266→            or an empty byte string if no additional data is available.
   267→        """
   268→
   269→        # NOTE(kgriffs): Yield to other tasks to give them a chance to
   270→        #   send us more body chunks if any are available.
   271→        #
   272→        #   https://bugs.python.org/issue34476
   273→        #
   274→        await asyncio.sleep(0)
   275→
   276→        if self._chunk_pos >= len(self._chunks):
   277→            return b''
   278→
   279→        data = b''.join(self._chunks[self._chunk_pos :])
   280→        self._chunk_pos = len(self._chunks)
   281→
   282→        return data

   285→class Result(_ResultBase):
   286→    """Encapsulates the result of a simulated request.
   287→
   288→    Args:
   289→        iterable (iterable): An iterable that yields zero or more
   290→            bytestrings, per PEP-3333
   291→        status (str): An HTTP status string, including status code and
   292→            reason string
   293→        headers (list): A list of (header_name, header_value) tuples,
   294→            per PEP-3333
   295→
   296→    Attributes:
   297→        status (str): HTTP status string given in the response
   298→        status_code (int): The code portion of the HTTP status string
   299→        headers (CaseInsensitiveDict): A case-insensitive dictionary
   300→            containing all the headers in the response, except for
   301→            cookies, which may be accessed via the `cookies`
   302→            attribute.
   303→
   304→            Note:
   305→
   306→                Multiple instances of a header in the response are
   307→                currently not supported; it is unspecified which value
   308→                will "win" and be represented in `headers`.
   309→
   310→        cookies (dict): A dictionary of
   311→            :py:class:`falcon.testing.Cookie` values parsed from the
   312→            response, by name.
   313→        encoding (str): Text encoding of the response body, or ``None``
   314→            if the encoding can not be determined.
   315→        content (bytes): Raw response body, or ``bytes`` if the
   316→            response body was empty.
   317→        text (str): Decoded response body of type ``str``.
   318→            If the content type does not specify an encoding, UTF-8 is
   319→            assumed.
   320→        json (JSON serializable): Deserialized JSON body. Will be ``None`` if
   321→            the body has no content to deserialize. Otherwise, raises an error
   322→            if the response is not valid JSON.
   323→    """
   324→
   325→    def __init__(self, iterable, status, headers):
   326→        super().__init__(status, headers)
   327→
   328→        self._text = None
   329→        self._content = b''.join(iterable)
   330→
   331→    @property
   332→    def content(self) -> bytes:
   333→        return self._content
   334→
   335→    @property
   336→    def text(self) -> str:
   337→        if self._text is None:
   338→            if not self.content:
   339→                self._text = ''
   340→            else:
   341→                if self.encoding is None:
   342→                    encoding = 'UTF-8'
   343→                else:
   344→                    encoding = self.encoding
   345→
   346→                self._text = self.content.decode(encoding)
   347→
   348→        return self._text
   349→
   350→    @property
   351→    def json(self) -> Optional[Union[dict, list, str, int, float, bool]]:
   352→        if not self.text:
   353→            return None
   354→
   355→        return json_module.loads(self.text)
   356→
   357→    def __repr__(self):
   358→        content_type = self.headers.get('Content-Type', '')
   359→
   360→        if len(self.content) > 40:
   361→            content = self.content[:20] + b'...' + self.content[-20:]
   362→        else:
   363→            content = self.content
   364→
   365→        args = [self.status, content_type, str(content)]
   366→
   367→        repr_result = ' '.join(filter(None, args))
   368→        return 'Result<{}>'.format(repr_result)

    18→            If req_range is ``None`` or ignored, content-range will be
    19→            ``None``; otherwise, the stream will be appropriately seeked and
    20→            possibly bounded, and the content-range will be a tuple of
    21→            (start, end, size).
    22→    """
    23→    fh = io.open(file_path, 'rb')

    26→        return fh, size, None
    27→
    28→    start, end = req_range
    29→    if size == 0:
    30→        # NOTE(tipabu): Ignore Range headers for zero-byte files; just serve
    31→        #   the empty body since Content-Range can't be used to express a
    32→        #   zero-byte body.
    33→        return fh, 0, None
    34→
    35→    if start < 0 and end == -1:
    36→        # NOTE(tipabu): Special case: only want the last N bytes.

    38→        fh.seek(start, os.SEEK_END)

    52→        #   servers for open files with a non-zero offset.

    61→class _BoundedFile:
    62→    """Wrap a file to only allow part of it to be read.
    63→
    64→    Args:
    65→        fh: The file object to wrap. Should be opened in binary mode,
    66→            and already seeked to an appropriate position. The object must
    67→            expose a ``.close()`` method.
    68→        length (int): Number of bytes that may be read.
    69→    """
    70→
    71→    def __init__(self, fh, length):
    72→        self.fh = fh
    73→        self.close = fh.close
    74→        self.remaining = length
    75→
    76→    def read(self, size=-1):
    77→        """Read the underlying file object, within the specified bounds."""
    78→        if size < 0:
    79→            size = self.remaining
    80→        else:
    81→            size = min(size, self.remaining)
    82→        data = self.fh.read(size)
    83→        self.remaining -= len(data)
    84→        return data
